newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Cowen ups Texas Instruments.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Cowen ups Texas Instruments.

text.p: -- Cowen & Co analyst Drew Peck said he plans to raise his 1997 year earnings estimate on Texas Instruments Inc by about $0.50 per share to reflect the impact of its new royalty licensing deal with Samsung Electronics Co Ltd.

-- The analyst said he expected the deal, which Texas Instruments valued at more than $1 billion over the next 10 years, to add about $35 million to Texas Instruments's quarterly earnings on an ongoing basis.
-- He estimated that Texas Instruments was currently receiving about $70 million in royalties per quarter from semiconductor cross-licensing deals with other chip makers.
-- Peck said his estimates are based the company's expectation that it will receive a larger share of the $1 billion-plus revenues in the first five years of the deal.

-- Based on conversations with the company, Drew said its willingness to predict it would receive more than $1 billion in revenues during the life of the agreement led him to believe Samsung has agreed to a floor level of royalties, independent of unit production or pricing variables.
-- As a result, Peck said he believes the royalty deal should reduce Texas Instruments's exposure to the volatility of the commodity computer memory chip market.
Pricing in this market has plummeted in the past year and demand historically has proven difficult to judge.

-- This will help Texas Instruments to pursue its stated goal of shifting more of its business into its higher-value digital signal processor business and away from its reliance on commodity semiconductor chips, he said.
-- Peck's prior estimate for Texas Instruments's 1997 year operating earnings was $3.14 per share. He maintains a buy rating on the stock.
